docs/guides/native-reference-render.md.text:
# Native reference-render publication

`StreamReferenceRenderPublication` publishes an original curatorial observation of
an actual native collection snapshot and the first and last retained mint serials.
It never changes the script, content root, Router, entropy, artist identity, or
rendering authority. This is the COLLECTION / ONCHAIN / still / BYTE_EXACT profile.
It requires both curator-declared STATIC artwork and one fixed registered STATIC
renderer declaration. Other scopes, DYNAMIC, PERCEPTUAL, CURATED and other capture
classes remain required profiles; a successful still does not establish them.

## Original authority and retained meaning

The new observed-reference type is explicitly allocated to the existing CURATOR
family. An actual Metadata collection class-3 grant takes precedence over global
scope-0 class-8. Both grant revision and original recorder are retained. Snapshot
class-7/8 authority does not authorize this record. Revoking a grant prevents new
publication without rewriting an admitted original. Curator classification is an
attributed assertion, not artist authorship, proof of arbitrary JavaScript being
static, or satisfaction of a renderer registration static-analysis/golden gate.

The constructor binds Core, Metadata, Schema, Store, Router, Snapshots and the
external-object coverage host by address and runtime hash. It also binds exactly
one renderer catalog ID, hash and full byte length. Deployment only checks the
fixed early getters and original Metadata Executor runtime pin; it does not read
current sources, a Coordinator, discovery, Finality or a future Registry. A caller
cannot choose a different STATIC catalog for a renderer already declared DYNAMIC.
Complete active original schema/profile/catalog bytes are reconstructed from the
actual registry and immutable Store at publication and current consumption.

The original manifest retains all package and platform-prerequisite rows, both
full sample HTML documents, original coverage tuples, source pins, actual original
coordinators and finalized seed values, the snapshot binding, and original
publication attribution. The renderer declaration pins the actual renderer
runtime, Router module version/manifest, context, presentation and dependency
read-set. Full original first/last checkpoint leaves are joined to Core identity
and historical Router JSON. Retained burned endpoints remain applicable; live
supply and ownerOf do not select the sample. Unresolved entropy cannot become a
zero default. A genuinely finalized zero seed is retained as such.

Package and platform file arrays are prepared separately through permissionless
`prepareFileInventory` calls. Each preparation validates and renders the entire
ordered array, retains its exact JSON in the actual Store, and uses a key committing
domain, chain, host, relative/absolute interpretation and every complete ABI row.
It creates no reference head, writer grant, archive receipt or publication clock.
An identical prepared key is immutable and can be reused only after its bytes pass
integrity checks. Final publication requires the exact keys of both supplied arrays
and checks all ordinary current source, archive and curator predicates atomically.
The final complete JSON is unchanged; no file is omitted to save transaction gas.

Whole canonical manifest bytes and the complete canonical ABI Publication are
retained through actual Store chunks. Every read checks exact length, STOP prefix,
per-chunk digest and full digest. Uploading chunks gives no writer authority.
The JSON payload and the original ABI witness must each fit the Store reader's
524,288-byte bound; fitting the JSON bound alone does not admit a larger ABI witness.
`referenceRecord` returns exactly `abi.encode(Publication, Receipt)` at the ABI
boundary, using the linked decoder with explicit original storage references.
No storage overlay or caller-chosen storage root is used.

Linked source and outer-JSON calls receive explicit projections containing only
the original fields those functions read. The projections omit file-array copies
from those calls; the complete original arrays still determine the preparation
keys, full environment bytes, original record hash and retained ABI witness. The
prior complete outer serializer is retained as a test oracle for exact output
equality. These projections create no alternate source of authority or content.
The two publication entrypoints decode the complete input once into memory; their
internal readers do not mutate that original. This preserves the external ABI and
avoids repeated full-array decoding before the original record is retained.

The record hash commits its domain, chain, publisher host, Core, Metadata, complete
Publication and complete Receipt with `recordHash` and `recordChainHash` zero.
`recordedAt` is included in that outer record preimage. The JSON manifest excludes
these later receipt fields. The environment excludes its own hash/length, which
the outer manifest commits. Snapshot head/revision and publication predecessor
are original provenance; later head/freeze bits do not enter immutable content.
Publication requires exact expected head/revision and source hash, and unique
per-collection reference IDs. Appending neither mutates nor deletes prior records.

## Runtime package and offchain correspondence

The actual runnable engine and named capture toolchain are archived as a complete
external ZIP object. A small descriptor or package manifest cannot substitute for
its whole-object byte size, SHA-256, Keccak and native Arweave data root. Each PNG
is also a complete covered object. The original two-family evidence requires an
ENDOWED Arweave inclusion slot and a distinct institutional possession slot plus
passing independent full-retrieval fixity. The exact proof model is documented in
[external-object archive](external-object-archive.md): quorum anchoring and signed
full-object observations are explicit trust boundaries, not Ethereum recomputing
all external file bytes or verifying native network consensus.

`tools.preservation.reference_manifest` validates canonical declared manifest
consistency, the pinned original native snapshot and complete preserved leaf
manifest, every actual ZIP member and whole-object digest/native root, actual
Router JSON to HTML to both capture files, and recorded loaded-module inventories.
It does not infer a live writer grant from local files or authenticate that an
observation was made by an independent human. The existing packaged capture tool
runs two fresh browser processes, rejects its unsupported features and resource
requests, preserves source/capture bytes and loaded modules, and compares actual
PNG bytes. These guards do not prove arbitrary executable JavaScript dependency
closure or artwork classification.

The native environment is Windows/AMD64, a named exact OS version, software raster,
sRGB and DPR 1, with bounded explicit viewport dimensions. Package rows include
all executable/toolchain files; platform rows name external OS/loader/system DLL
requirements. No self-contained OS image claim is made. Onchain lexical checks
preserve ASCII relative paths and byte order; full Windows reserved-name and
case-alias checks belong to the offline package validator. ZIP member containment
and execution correspondence remain the curator's original attributed declaration
corroborated by the retained local checks, not onchain ZIP parsing or execution.

The preserved proprietary-browser license basis is `undetermined`, with its exact
original license note. This code increment authorizes no public binary upload or
redistribution. Redistribution licensing must be resolved before any such upload.

## Current consumption, locks and availability

Current consumption revalidates the actual graph, definitions, snapshot/source
facts and complete retained bytes. It uses the exact two original receipt hashes
for each object and compares every stable identity field. Later passing fixity
heads may restore current availability for those same receipts after the defined
failure/repair process. They cannot choose replacement receipts, another object,
family, locator, profile or artist. Saved original coverage is used in the source
hash, so routine PASS refresh does not change locked reference content. Current
coverage has no annual/quarterly scheduler or elapsed freshness gate; that broader
preservation cadence remains separate.

The host-local one-way reference lock requires the pinned actual Executor's exact
current class-2 action, scope, old and new transition hashes. It first validates
the selected current original. The lock cannot authorize other record families,
freeze generic Metadata, or supply artist content consent. Unlocked current reads
are distinct from locked current component readiness.

The host directly implements collection and scoped artwork finality component
interfaces, returning REFERENCE_RENDER only for the canonical collection scope.
Its component data hash commits original Receipt and Lock and excludes refreshed
passing fixity heads. Its constructor has no provider/Registry runtime cycle.

`StreamFinalityReferenceReads` pins Core, Metadata, Router, Snapshots and publisher.
It corroborates the publisher's exact canonical 20-word current receipt and
four-word lock, preserving original attribution, effective/recorded timestamps,
predecessor/revision and definition commitments. `requireCurrent` exposes unlocked
status; `requireLocked` requires the exact populated current lock. It relies on
the pinned publisher's original full variable-witness admission and current source
reconstruction; it does not independently rebuild that large original preimage.
A passing input is not aggregate finality, archive cadence, institutional acceptance
or complete runtime portability.

## Publication sequence

1. Register the exact schema/profile/format documents and the fixed renderer
   declaration. Deploy the publisher against its early immutable dependencies.
2. Obtain the current original Snapshot and complete retained mint inventory.
   Export the historical Router JSON for its first and last serials, preserving
   every byte of the native HTML and the original seed/token-data commitments.
3. Capture both samples with the archived toolchain, retain both repeated PNGs and
   execution reports, and verify the complete package and loaded dependencies.
   Unsupported features require another profile; a failed capture is not a waiver.
4. Admit the complete runtime and capture objects through the external-object
   receipt/proof/fixity flow. The onchain object identities must refer to those
   actual complete files, with the same artist and two independent original slots.
5. Upload each file inventory's canonical JSON chunks to the fixed Store and call
   `prepareFileInventory` for the complete package and platform arrays. Those calls
   may use separate transactions and do not reserve a publication or grant.
6. Call `previewReference` with the full Publication and intended curator. Set its
   exact expected source hash, retain the returned canonical JSON and the complete
   `abi.encode(Publication)` in the Store, then call `publishReference` as that
   authorized curator. A changed head, source or archive state causes atomic failure.
7. Read the original receipt/payload and verify current state separately. The exact
   staged terminal transition may lock the current record; only the locked current
   publication supplies the direct finality component.

The offline command is `python -m tools.preservation.reference_manifest`. Its
required inputs are the original manifest and an independently retained expected
Keccak anchor, `--snapshot-manifest` containing the original native snapshot JSON,
`--leaf-manifest` containing the complete canonical binary
[content leaf manifest](../integrations/content-leaf-manifests.md), complete runtime
ZIP, the report's restored runtime root, and one `--metadata` /
`--capture-directory` pair per required sample. The Python API likewise requires
`validate(raw, snapshot_bytes=..., leaf_manifest_bytes=...)`; its caller must
independently anchor `raw`. It reads the archived tool's literal controls without
executing that source during validation. Its
output explicitly reports local byte consistency separately from live authority,
network inclusion and execution attestation.

The reference pins the snapshot bytes, which pin the leaf bytes, checkpoint
producer, plan, count, ordered leaf chain and content root. The offline verifier
recomputes both commitments from every leaf, rejects repeated, missing or reordered
leaves, and matches captures to the exact first and last token IDs and their
metadata, HTML and token-data hashes. A singleton has one capture. Token IDs and
collection serials may have gaps after incident abort; `mintedEver` is an inventory
count, not the last serial. Burned completed tokens remain in this historical
inventory and need no live owner lookup.

The six-word content leaf does not contain a collection serial or lifecycle flag.
Those facts remain committed statements from the independently anchored reference,
whose original publication checked Core identity. After authenticating endpoint
membership, the offline verifier checks positive, increasing declared serials; it
does not independently verify Core serials or whether an endpoint was burned.
Changing a capture's serial changes the original manifest anchor.

## Validation and explicit fixture boundaries

The actual composition uses the real Snapshot, Metadata, Schema/Store, Router,
original-coordinator inventory and native policy readers, leaf checkpoint/manifest,
RoleRegistry, external-object coverage/checkpoint proof and upstream threshold
Safe. Core, Executor, artist/seed authority, the older leaf archive boundary and
network/institution/fixity observations are explicitly named fixtures. Local
signed observations do not constitute public archival delivery.

The full original browser package and first/last actual Router exports are retained
in the immutable delivery evidence directory. The earlier 447-byte local HTML
sample is only tool smoke; reference publication tests use actual exported Router
bytes and newly authorized original reference records. The complete 253,440,410-byte
ZIP has 364 members (including PACKAGE.json), with 108 explicit platform
prerequisites. The two source HTML documents are 447 bytes each; their repeated
PNG objects are 198 and 199 bytes. The emitted canonical manifest is 83,420 bytes
and is independently joined to those complete archive and capture files.

The matching actual composition passes 19 IR tests, including two 256-run
properties, original record/retained ABI and prior serializer parity, malformed
input, rollback/retry, grant, archive, lock and Safe controls. Six serializer tests
pass in both compiler modes, including two 256-run properties per mode. The offline
validator passes 18 tests and the definition generator matches the registered bytes.
These are focused cohorts, not a complete repository or full-v1 conformance run.

Cached probes reuse the exact compiled actual sources without recompilation:

| Timed call | Ordinary test context | Foundry `--isolate` context |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Publication with an explicit 16,000,000-gas call bound | 13,529,647 | 15,878,615 |
| Complete fixed consumer, 18 named targets cooled | 5,850,221 | 6,152,221 |

The consumer returns exactly 576 bytes. Package preparation separately succeeds
at 12,337,566 timed gas in the final actual cohort. The earlier isolated Safe publication trace
records 16,047,696 at its outer proxy, 15,114,663 at its implementation and
14,997,230 at the publisher. Those nested figures are not additive. Its inner
publication calldata is 105,700 bytes; its separately calculated Paris intrinsic
cost is 902,368. That calculation is not added to the isolated trace charges.
The probes preserve their actual envelopes and named-account cooling; they do
not establish all-account cold execution, another batch/transaction context,
all permitted inventory sizes, or another network's current gas rules.

The final Safe envelope test uses the complete `execTransaction` calldata and
ordinary two-of-two ECDSA signatures. For its isolated run, the 106,276 bytes
contain 67,900 zero and 38,376 nonzero bytes. With empty access/authorization lists,
zero value and no contract creation, intrinsic gas is 906,616 and the calldata
floor is 2,235,040. The floor is a minimum total, not a second deduction from the
execution budget. These formulas follow [EIP-7623](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7623).

The test forwards exactly 15,870,600 gas, the
[EIP-7825 limit](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7825) of 16,777,216 minus that
intrinsic cost, to the actual Safe proxy. The CALL-inclusive execution measurement
is 15,163,821; the resulting envelope is 16,070,437, leaving 706,779 gas. It checks
low-level success, canonical Safe `true`, the nonce increment and the original
class-8 publication. A preceding insufficient-gas call leaves the nonce and
publication unchanged, and the identical signed request then succeeds. The
ordinary-context run is retained separately with its own exact encoded bytes;
its byte counts and gas charges are not substituted into the isolated calculation.

This is a Paris-compiled and Paris-executed entry-gas simulation under Foundry
`--isolate`, with sufficient wrapper gas to avoid EIP-150 truncation. The test
wrapper's decoder and entry overhead are outside the simulated transaction to
the Safe. It is not a raw transaction receipt, proof of another execution fork's
equivalence, or a capacity bound for every supported inventory. Both probes reuse
the matching compiled sources without recompilation. All standalone default and
IR production runtimes fit EIP-170; the evidence separately records the fixed
reader's six-byte IR scratch-allocation variation between compiler contexts.

docs/guides/external-object-archive.md.text:
# External whole-object archive evidence

`StreamExternalArtifactCoverage` is a separate bulk-object preservation backend.
It preserves the whole external object's Keccak256, SHA256, native Arweave data
root and uint64 byte size. The descriptor's bytes never stand in for those bytes.
Existing bounded ArchivalCoverage, ArweaveInclusion and ArtifactCoverage profiles
keep their existing meaning and implementation.

This backend implements the external-object allowance in LTA-CATALOGS rule 4
and the original-receipt and independent-fixity joins of LTA-FINALITY rule 11
and LTA-ARCHIVE rules 1–3. It is a prerequisite for reference-render publication;
it does not itself establish reference-render, finality or full preservation
program conformance.

## Original evidence

1. Anyone may retain an object declaration. Its schema, canonicalization and
   format/catalog values are unverified declarations at this stage. A consuming
   record profile must authenticate the complete registered definitions and
   selected format entry. Declaration alone creates no archival coverage.
2. The actual governed family admission pins taxonomy dimensions and the storing
   agent. Endowed rows require the named Arweave mainnet external-object quorum
   profile; institutional rows require the named HTTPS possession profile.
   Same-name rows are separately admitted immutable taxonomy versions. They do
   not imply a latest version and cannot count as distinct families.
3. Each original receipt is signed by its family's storing agent, through EOA,
   bounded ERC1271, or the actual direct caller. The exact locator and signature
   are retained. A direct Safe call identifies that Safe as the storing agent.
   The endowed locator is the exact 32-byte transaction ID. The institutional
   locator is a closed ASCII HTTPS/DNS-label form with a nonempty path; there is
   no DNS, availability, TLS or retrieval assertion from syntax validation.
4. `StreamArweaveObjectCheckpointVerifier` authenticates an observer quorum's
   transaction-ID/root association under its own configuration and EIP712 domain.
   Native annotated Merkle paths prove the declared transaction range, data root,
   object size, and first/last chunk endpoints. Full proof paths and the original
   observer certificate remain available. This is explicitly a named quorum
   trust model, not an Ethereum verification of native network consensus.
5. A separately authorized `ROLE_FIXITY_OPERATOR`, distinct from the receipt
   writer, signs exact expected **and** observed whole-file SHA256, Keccak256,
   native data root and byte size, plus the original receipt, object, family,
   locator, profile, report, predecessor and replay fields. Passing fixity
   requires all four observed values to equal the declared object. The operator
   is attesting to full retrieval and computation; Ethereum does not read the
   complete external file. Native endpoint paths alone do not establish either
   flat hash or validate omitted middle bytes.

Both receipt and fixity signatures use the new coverage contract's EIP712
domain. Checkpoint signatures use the new checkpoint contract's separate domain.
Original evidence and signatures survive role revocation. A new fixity requires
the current role. Receipt deadlines govern admission, not historical expiry.

## Current coverage and repair

Coverage needs exactly an endowed inclusion receipt and an institutional
possession receipt for the same full object. Family identity, network, protocol,
addressing, custodian, funding, retrieval and storing agent must be distinct;
jurisdiction may coincide. These are governed declarations, not an inference of
real-world organizational independence.

Both receipts must have latest passing fixity. A later failure invalidates old
coverage without deleting it. A subsequent pass requires an explicit repair
report and exact latest-fixity predecessor; recording a new coverage entry never
rewrites the old entry. Each current read rechecks pinned Core, Executor, roles,
checkpoint graph/configuration, active family status and both latest fixities.
This is not an annual/quarterly scheduler or a cadence gate. The preservation
program must separately enforce due dates and cycles.

The Core/module/Executor graph is fixed independently of caller-supplied object
metadata. Family admission/status changes require the actual class-1 current
governance action with its exact scope and old/new state hashes. Gas parameters
are separately governed for fixed-size reads and signature verification.


The additive `IStreamExternalArtifactCurrentPair.currentReceiptPair` returns
fourteen unsaved current facts for two explicitly supplied **original receipt
hashes**, expected artist and expected whole object. It reuses the exact same
context, independent-family, native-checkpoint and latest-passing-fixity checks.
It does not record coverage, choose another receipt or change `requireCoverage`:
even a later PASS still makes an old recorded coverage fail that original exact
head check. Current availability can recover after an authorized failure/repair
chain for the same receipts without rewriting a locked reference publication.

A reference consumer must retain the original coverage and both original
receipt/fixity identities in its immutable record. At every current read it must
compare this new pair's complete object, artist, profile, family, receipt and
checkpoint identities to those saved originals; only the latest fixity hashes
may differ. Those later observations are current evidence, never retroactively
part of the original publication hash. Family suspension and changed pinned
graph still fail immediately. Original signer role revocation does not erase
admission; a new fixity requires the current role. This read adds no elapsed-age
freshness rule or annual/quarterly cadence scheduler.

## Runnable fixture and limits

The public test fixture identifies a real locally packaged 253,440,410-byte
Windows browser/toolchain archive, not a reduced browser descriptor. Independent
upstream chunking reconstructs all 967 native chunks and the root used by the
contract tests. The archive's flat SHA256 is
`d2eabd7dffeed4f37632e9e8d5a861d7fe5df621d66e62cd43234ecb9a572417`.
Its native storage root is a distinct value. No raw-CID equality is inferred.

The archive has been restored from its complete ordered transport parts and run
from that fresh folder. The test's observer network checkpoint, institutional
receipt and fixity signers are explicit local fixtures. They demonstrate actual
contract execution with the real object's commitments; they are not public
Arweave upload, institutional acceptance, public delivery or independent human
verification. The native Windows environment has separately pinned OS/runtime
prerequisites and an undetermined proprietary-browser license basis; it is not
a self-contained operating-system image or a permission to redistribute Chrome.

The actual RoleRegistry composition follows the IR compiler route. The new
production contracts and isolated native proof tests compile in both profiles.
The current-read probe cools five named contracts and measures a 2M-gas callee
budget; it is not complete cold finality-provider capacity. Reference-render
source/sample/classification, complete registered schema/format interpretation,
sale-follows deadlines, archival cadence, actual public delivery and final
aggregate consumption remain separate admission work.

docs/integrations/reference-inventory-pr.text:
# Reference environment inventory preparation

The inventory serializer preserves the original canonical JSON, row ordering,
path validation and errors. It writes each row into one final output buffer;
relative paths use the original printable-ASCII restrictions, while absolute
paths retain the original UTF-8 and JSON quoting routine. Decimal quantities
remain strings and SHA-256 digests remain lowercase, fixed-width hex strings.

The isolated 26-source Solidity 0.8.19 capture passes eight tests, including
three sets of 256 differential fuzz cases against the frozen prior serializer,
every possible relative-path byte, zero/max quantities, duplicate and unordered
rows, and original size/error boundaries. The final closing bracket convention
is preserved, including the original maximum-length edge case.

The retained actual corpus contains 1,048 package members and 102 explicit
platform prerequisites. Their exact JSON lengths remain 162,109 and 15,583 bytes.
Measured direct-call package gas falls from 33,479,092 to 18,145,166; platform gas
falls from 4,084,702 to 3,102,427. These measurements include the test caller's
call overhead, not transaction calldata intrinsic gas. The package call alone
still exceeds the 16,777,216 transaction envelope, before host preparation and
retention. This optimization does not establish a usable complete preparation
transaction. A separate authenticated staged preparation flow is required.

No inventory identity, schema, hash domain, storage layout, writer authority,
gas cap or current-source check changes in this serializer batch. These tests
do not demonstrate a completed mode publication or a full current-stack flow.

## Authenticated staged preparation

`IStreamReferenceInventoryPreparation` is an additive companion implemented by
both reference publication hosts. The original publication interface IDs,
monolithic preparation methods and whole-inventory identities remain unchanged.
The new fixed worker receives the host's compiler-declared inventory mapping;
neither host adds storage.

1. Split the full original rows into consecutive groups of 64, with a final
   remainder of 1 through 64 rows. Preserve every original path, quantity and
   digest. Each group is encoded as its own canonical JSON array.
2. Preupload the exact part-array and complete-array bytes to the existing
   `StreamSchemaDocumentStore`, in ordered chunks of at most 8,192 bytes.
   Each upload is a separate zero-value call if required by transaction capacity.
3. Call `prepareFileInventoryPart(rows,relative)` for each group. It validates
   original row rules, authenticates preuploaded bytes and retains immutable
   pointers. Its part identity is `keccak256(abi.encode(domain,chainId,host,
   relative,rows))`, where `domain` is the Keccak of
   `6529STREAM_REFERENCE_FILE_INVENTORY_PART_V1`.
4. Call `prepareFileInventoryFromParts(fullOriginalRows,relative)`. The caller
   does not supply part IDs or totals. The producer derives every exact part
   identity from those full rows, checks boundary ordering and size limits,
   reconstructs the complete original JSON array, and authenticates its Store
   chunks. The resulting identity retains the original
   `6529STREAM_REFERENCE_FILE_INVENTORY_V1` domain and full-row preimage.
5. Use the original `preparedFileInventory(id)` readback and publication flow.

An empty full inventory uses zero parts and the exact preuploaded `[]` bytes.
Empty parts and parts larger than 64 rows are rejected. Part identities bind the
current host, chain and relative-path flag. Permissionless preparation creates
no writer, archive or source authority and does not establish that a caller's
declared environment lists every external package member.

Existing intact identities are idempotent and return without a new preparation
event. First successful writes emit schema-1 `ReferenceInventoryPartPrepared`
or `ReferenceInventoryAssembled`; a late missing chunk reverts every write and
event. The part and original domains share the existing mapping without letting
a part substitute for an original full-inventory identity.

The focused 30-source worker/Store capture passes six cases, including the full
1,048-row corpus, swapped/omitted/duplicate/truncated/substituted inputs, host,
chain and relative-flag mismatches, existing identities and late missing-chunk
rollback followed by retry. Its guarded test host passes an actual
compiler-declared mapping to the real worker and Store; it is not a complete
reference publication host. The test explicitly cools its host, linked workers,
Store and recorded chunk pointers before the bounded calls.

For that corpus, measured transaction envelopes including ordinary calldata
intrinsic gas are 1,877,011 maximum for complete-array chunk uploads, 1,770,416
maximum for part preparation, and 12,768,072 for final assembly. Every tested
chunk upload and part call also enforces the 16,777,216 bound individually.
These results cover the recorded corpus, not every permitted maximum-length
path, all future gas schedules or a fully cold current protocol graph.

The affected production hosts and worker pass a separate 125-source ABI check
and selected size measurement: original host runtime 20,833 bytes, mode host
22,810, and worker 4,052. Actual publication-host runtime integration remains
pending. The independent reference publication decoder/copy capacity failure
recorded in the metric supplement guide also remains unresolved; this staged
preparation result does not waive it.

## Prepared canonical environments

`IStreamReferenceEnvironmentPreparation` adds
`prepareEnvironment(Environment)`. First prepare the two exact original full
file inventories, then upload the original complete canonical environment
bytes to the same Store in 8,192-byte chunks. The guarded host delegates to a
fixed worker which authenticates those inventories, runs the original field
validation and canonical builder, and checks the supplied manifest hash and
length before retaining the bytes. The builder now concatenates the same
ordered fragments into one exact-size buffer; its field order, quoting and
limit remain unchanged.

The preparation ID is `keccak256(abi.encode(domain, chainId, host, environment))`,
where `domain` is `keccak256("6529STREAM_REFERENCE_ENVIRONMENT_PREPARATION_V1")`.
All fields of the original typed Environment participate, including both full
file arrays and the coverage reference. The identity uses the actual
publication host, not the preparer or the worker. The original inventory and
record domains and storage layout remain unchanged. The new domain shares
the compiler-declared inventory mapping; `preparedFileInventory(id)` reads
its complete retained bytes. First successful retention emits schema-1
`ReferenceEnvironmentPrepared`; an intact repeated identity emits no event.
Missing late chunks revert all state and events before identical retry.

The mode preparation caller derives this same ID from its actual complete
typed input. If a prepared environment exists, it checks and reads its exact
immutable bytes. Otherwise the original environment construction remains the
fallback. No caller supplies an alternate preparation ID. This reuses only
deterministic canonical bytes; original writer authorization, dependency
selection/runtime checks, current sources, archival coverage, mode evidence
and finality checks still execute in their original flow. Preparation does
not attest that an environment ran, or prove its coverage reference current.

The initial environment preparation probe failed its unchanged transaction
envelope during final chunk retention. The exact-buffer successor passes the
focused original-body comparisons, malformed/oversized/error cases, 256 fuzz
inputs, complete 1,048/102-row corpus, host/chain/full-input separation,
eventless idempotence, missing-chunk rollback and retained-byte corruption
controls. Its real Store and fixed worker operate through a minimal guarded
host. Complete production-host execution and the complete publisher envelope
remain separate acceptance requirements; no cap or minimum budget changed.

The final focused 31-source capture passes eight tests and 256 fuzz cases.
For the recorded corpus, preparation uses 13,936,415 gas including ordinary
calldata intrinsic cost. A separate projected-read call uses 7,749,281 including
intrinsic cost; it builds calldata before measurement and excludes the test
caller's later returndata copy. That read number is not the cost of the whole
mode-preparation caller or its preceding evidence checks. The tests identify
the accounts and stored chunk pointers they cool; these measurements are not
a universal cold-graph or all-permitted-input guarantee.

The changed products fit selected pinned compiler settings: original host
21,095-byte runtime, mode host 23,274, inventory/environment worker 7,753 and
mode preparation worker 23,157. Existing host ABI entries and recursive
storage layouts are preserved; only the new companion function and event are
added. Whole publisher/Safe/lock/inventory transaction acceptance still needs
the joined source capture. The separately retained payload-inlining experiment
was not adopted: its parity tests passed, but its preparation runtime exceeded
the deployment limit.

docs/guides/preservation-inventory.md.text:
# Render-critical inventory and archival bundle coverage

This implementation materializes a finite inventory from the actual native
collection source graph. The inventory and its archival coverage are separate
evidence. A content-leaf coverage hash, source inventory hash, or reference
manifest hash cannot substitute for either result.

The supported profile is an artist-associated COLLECTION scope with the native
onchain renderer and the admitted STATIC/BYTE_EXACT reference-render publication. Dynamic,
perceptual, curated, other scope families, and arbitrary JavaScript dependency
closure remain separate implementation obligations. An attributed STATIC
declaration does not prove that arbitrary JavaScript has no runtime dependencies.

## Original inputs and deployment

`StreamRenderCriticalInventory` binds the selected original content root,
snapshot, reference render, intent or intent waiver, interview status, RIGHTS,
and WORK evidence. An explicit interview waiver commits its authenticated
parent declaration and produces no invented interview original. Estate material
does not replace the selected original artist lineage. Historical author and
original publication grants retain their existing producer meanings.
The native presentation and conservation selection must agree on the fixed
artist registry/runtime, artist ID, binding generation, binding hash, and
original identity record. A shared artist ID alone cannot join different
original associations. The original nominated key is not substituted for an
original record signer; rotation and delegated publication remain distinct.

The dependencies are constructor-only storage. They include Core, generic
Metadata, Schema, Store, Router, the three typed selectors, Snapshot, Reference,
both archival providers, and the original Artist facade/Coordinator/Identity/
Attribution/Archive/Content owner pins. Construction does not query later
selection or a future complete finality provider. Runtime checks authenticate
the completed fixed graph. There is no callback from inventory into the
complete provider's finality-input read.

The eight inputs exclude these two new evidence outputs, the later finality
manifest, and its later sanction/signature archives. Those later objects retain
their independent original admission and archival gates. Exclusion avoids a
circular hash preimage; it is not an archival exemption.

## Materialization and current consumption

`beginInventory(collectionId)` derives a plan from the complete current original
context. Permissionless stages append native source bytes, the original
reference environment, typed WORK and RIGHTS, typed intent/waiver and interview,
the original content-root authorization, all 31 fixed interpretation documents,
and every token in the retained minted-ever inventory. Burned tokens remain
members. Each stage checks the fixed source graph and the relevant original
record. Final sealing repeats the full current-context comparison.

Every segment has a host/chain/plan/index-bound key, a source witness commitment,
an exact count, and a backwards item chain. Each link includes its segment key,
index, count, complete typed item, and successor. A zero successor is permitted
exactly at the last index. Final consumption checks both the exact aggregate
count and ordered segment chain. Repeated bytes in distinct roles remain
distinct occurrences. A package member, the package itself, rendered HTML,
token metadata, and a content leaf are different objects.

Every interpretation document is reconstructed from the actual registered
ordered chunks at admission. Its complete nine-word facts are retained and
rechecked at seal/current use, including definitions not selected by the current
intent/waiver branch. `requireFullDefinitionBytes` is a stronger diagnostic that
also reconstructs every byte again. The ordinary current path relies on fixed
Registry/Store identity and ordinary EVM immutability of admitted STOP bytecode
for already authenticated bytes; it does not promise equivalence under arbitrary
test-state edits.

`requireCurrent(collectionId)` returns the 19-word inventory evidence, including
the exact eight originals, scope, source context, member inventory, counts,
complete segment chain, and independently derived `renderCriticalEvidenceHash`.
`inventoryEvidence(planId)` is a historical read and does not establish current
eligibility.

## Exact objects, references, and applicability

The typed walks preserve every supported original Reference and complete catalog,
including unselected catalog entries. Hash algorithm and canonicalization labels
remain part of identity even when two references describe the same bytes. The
first correspondence profile verifies Keccak-256 or SHA-256 for RAW_BYTES/JCS
where the selected backend exposes the exact corresponding object digest.
Unsupported nonempty methods fail explicitly. They cannot become absent or
inherit coverage of a descriptor. The six-algorithm serializer vocabulary remains
unchanged; additional actual correspondence methods remain required work.

Native source objects include actual script/display/configuration bytes,
renderer/Router/Core runtimes, the full snapshot, original content-root and leaf
manifest, the complete leaf-list artifact, every retained original Coordinator
runtime/policy, and each member's exact token data, metadata JSON, image
applicability, and animation HTML. Current native policy inventory is not an
oracle-output or arbitrary execution-closure proof.

The reference inventory retains the whole executable archive identity, every
ordered package-file identity, capture objects, complete environment declaration,
and named OS prerequisites. Whole-ZIP coverage remains independent from the
per-file coverage. Per-file digest correspondence does not itself prove ZIP
containment; membership is the original attributed manifest plus the separately
verified whole-ZIP inventory. The native Windows prerequisite branch is explicitly
unarchived OS applicability, not a self-contained archived operating system.

`EMPTY_PACKAGE_MEMBER` retains an original package path, member index, zero size,
and the exact SHA256 of empty bytes. The authenticated reference declaration
must contain that exact empty identity. It is intrinsically reconstructible;
no nonempty native object, storage receipt, or dual-family coverage is invented.
The actual 364-member package contains three such files and 361 nonempty files.
The offline `tools/preservation/inventory_package_objects.py` joins every ordered
uncompressed member to the externally anchored complete ZIP, reconstructs each
nonempty member's flat digests and native root/proofs, and retains empty members.
These local checks do not establish public network delivery or signer authority.

`EMPTY_BYTES` means the reader derived an exact empty authoritative field. It
binds RAW_BYTES/Keccak(empty)/length zero and is intrinsically reconstructible;
it is not dual-family coverage. `ABSENT` records an actual supported applicability
decision, such as no token image or an explicitly waived interview original. A
caller cannot select either branch for a nonempty authoritative value.

## Original signed bundles

The CMC-ATTESTATIONS state-retention branch is explicit `STATE_BUNDLE`. Op24
retention binds the complete original ArchiveV2 envelope, original publication,
the original attestation record preimage and signer/class/time, and exact generic
Metadata receipt. The external Coordinator actor is an untrusted archive locator,
not a substitute signer. Op17 separately binds the original Content owner record,
Router content-root record, exact consent statement and original observed time.
The signed deadline is not substituted for the observed record time. Historical
proof is not reauthorized against today's signer, nonce, grant, or ERC1271 owners.

Exact original archival receipts and fixities retain their full state-readable
terms, locators, signatures, checkpoint certificates/proofs, and envelope bytes.
The onchain artifact's additive `originalArtifactChunkCoverage(completion,index)`
returns its immutable original per-part evidence. Passing refresh never changes
that locator. This finite original bundle does not recursively demand another
archive of the new coverage proof itself.

## Archival admission and refresh

`StreamBundleArchiveCoverage` consumes the exact completed inventory plan. Each
`coverNext` call authenticates the next complete item and its suffix against the
saved segment chain, then verifies the applicable actual archive proof. External
objects require the same original two receipts, independent families, passing
fixity and full tuple correspondence. Onchain objects require actual whole-byte
artifact coverage, every ordered STOP child, exact original per-part coverage,
and the retained original signed bundles. A descriptor's coverage never proves
coverage of the described executable or another payload.

The separately named immutable-STOP aggregate profile records each admission
under a complete current environment. It seals the ordered evidence chain and
count. Current use rechecks the complete mutable environment and cache revision.
The external host's health revision advances atomically for every successful
family admission/status write and every latest-fixity write, including PASS to
PASS. Its environment includes the actual current graph/configuration/profile/
chain pins. Current-role revocation is not silently added to old receipt
semantics; no annual/quarterly cadence or timestamp expiry is invented.

An environment change during initial admission or refresh cannot certify a mix
of epochs. A permissionless ordered refresh must cover every saved item under
one unchanged environment. Later passing fixity can update current observation
evidence for the same original receipts while preserving the immutable bundle
commitment. Failed fixity, family health changes, changed graph/runtime, or an
incomplete refresh prevents current success.

`requireCoverage(planId, expectedRenderCriticalEvidenceHash)` returns five words:
the inventory plan, its render-critical commitment, exact item count, immutable
evidence chain, and independent `bundleCoverageHash`. It does not repeat source
currentness. The complete provider must call inventory current once and join this
exact corresponding plan/hash. `bundleEvidence` is historical.
`requireFullCurrentCoverage` is the full per-item diagnostic: external items reread
the same original pair/current fixity, and onchain items reread STOP parts and
original bundle bytes. These methods do not claim arbitrary etched-storage
equivalence.

## Validation boundary

The matching IR cohort passes all 31 named tests, including five 256-run
properties, the complete 547-role bundle through both archival backends, full
refresh, actual Safe calls, original-author preservation, and exact parity with
the earlier 479-item reference/event construction. Separate focused allocator
oracles pass in both compiler modes, including shared dynamic aliases, later
allocations, every default field, and the original ordered item encoding.
Earlier external-environment, native/original-bundle, and package-tool cohorts
retain their own frozen source and runtime identities.

For this fixture, current inventory uses 10,130,862 gas after cooling 25 named
targets, within its 16-million callee bound. The complete bundle's cached current
read uses 149,064 gas after cooling nine named targets, within its 3-million
callee bound. These are specified current reads, not whole-account cold or
complete provider transaction measurements. The full per-item diagnostic remains
separate from the cached consumption path.

The reference stage's isolated Safe envelope uses 612 bytes of canonical
`execTransaction` calldata and two ordinary ECDSA signatures. Independently
recomputed intrinsic gas is 25,800 and the calldata floor is 33,000. The measured
Safe execution, including the inner CALL overhead, is 15,097,963 gas; the total
envelope is 15,123,763, leaving 1,653,453 below 16,777,216. The test forwards only
the remaining entry budget and requires canonical Safe success, one nonce
increment, all 479 roles, and the unchanged original curator. This is a
Paris-compiled execution-entry simulation, not a raw network transaction receipt
or modern-fork equivalence proof. Its wrapper overhead is outside the simulated
direct-to-Safe transaction. Other publication stages and the complete provider
must retain their own transaction-envelope measurements.

This is a working supported-profile increment, not release or testnet readiness.
It does not establish arbitrary maximum-size capacity or complete current-stack
assembly. The fixture's Core/Artist/Executor/seed/network boundaries remain
explicit; real source, record, archive and Safe operations within those boundaries
do not turn them into independently authenticated deployed authorities. Exact
whole-object digests and locally signed archival observations do not imply a
public archival upload, independent human fixity observation, or a licensing
decision.

docs/integrations/scoped-render-critical.text:
# Scoped render-critical source inventory

`StreamScopedRenderCriticalInventory` is the distinct staged source producer
for TOKEN, RELEASE and SEASON. It does not implement the COLLECTION interface,
accept a collection receipt for another subject, or make membership into VIEW
adoption authority. It currently consumes the finalized-entropy STATIC profile;
terminal-entropy output needs its separately admitted output and snapshot
profile. The new host and traversal have an ABI/type check only. Their native
execution, size, transaction capacity, complete provider and finality ceremony
remain pending.

## Original source and plan identity

The constructor pins the same named Core, Metadata, Schema, Store, Router,
selection/membership, archive and Artist sources used by its fixed workers.
The snapshot and reference slots name the distinct scoped producers. Runtime
hashes and reciprocal joins are checked at operative reads; predicted late
addresses are not treated as already-live dependencies.

`beginInventory(scope)` derives its context from the actual current scoped
reference, complete snapshot and membership, authoritative scoped CONTENT_ROOT,
WORK/RIGHTS, and conservation selection. The plan domain is
`6529STREAM_SCOPED_RENDER_CRITICAL_PLAN_V1`, followed by chain, actual inventory
host, dependency hash and the complete context. Repeating the same current plan
returns its existing ID without another event. Callers do not supply the
source context, expected token count or segment list.

Each mutation refreshes that complete current source before its stage runs.
Evidence already completed remains readable historically; `requireCurrent`
requires the exact current context and active interpretation documents.
Permissionless preparation confers no publication, Artist, archive or finality
authority.

## Complete ordered traversal

The public interface is `IStreamScopedRenderCriticalInventory`. Its fixed order
is:

1. `appendNative(id, maximum)`: next 1–64 original native source/runtime rows.
2. `appendReference(id, maximum)`: next 1–64 reference rows, including every
   original package member, declared platform prerequisite and capture.
3. `appendWork`, then `appendRights`: exact selected typed records and bytes.
4. `appendIntent` or `appendIntentWaiver`, then `appendInterview` or its actual
   parent-bound waiver: the original selected conservation evidence.
5. `appendRootAuthorization`: original op17 Archive proof. Historical aggregate
   and legacy-family values are untrusted preimage witnesses, authenticated by
   the original scoped record and signed family state.
6. `appendDefinition`: every fixed required definition, in the producer's order.
7. For every authoritative membership ordinal, `appendTokenOutput`,
   `appendTokenScript`, `appendTokenLibrary`, every `appendTokenRenderer` row,
   then every `appendTokenCitation` row.
8. `sealInventory`: only after all source stages and every token's final row.

The token phase and row cursor are available through `tokenProgress(id)`.
There is no caller-selected next ordinal or expected row total. A token advances
only after its output, executable bytes, renderer evidence and optional current
citation evidence finish. Script and library workers verify every original
logical chunk plus the complete ordered payload; empty/absent declarations
remain explicit occurrences. Full output uses the checkpoint's exact current
`tokenJSON` and `tokenHTML` selectors, with the finite profile bounds of 65,536
JSON, 40,960 HTML and 2,048 image bytes. Larger outputs are not silently truncated
or accepted as complete.

Native/reference totals come from the authenticated original records. A small
segment limit never turns a capture sample into complete membership or a partial
ZIP member list into complete environment evidence. Token ordinals retain Core's
actual global token ID, permanent collection serial and burned lifecycle; they
are not converted to serial plus one. Empty/incomplete membership refuses this
reference-dependent profile.

## Current citation evidence

An original renderer without the capability contributes one explicit ABSENT
occurrence. A capable renderer must have the separate, actual current-base-
citation admission. The inventory includes its complete 12-word registration
record, exact superset of the original read declarations, actual registered
analysis/golden bytes, and pinned encoding runtime. It independently rebuilds
the original read-set and registration hashes and checks the exact profile,
selector, chain, Schema registry and saved original version.

The complete original renderer target roster and its original five documents
remain mandatory separate rows. Current citation evidence does not replace
those original goldens or create terminal-entropy admission. Actual selected
renderer/citation document facts are deduplicated by document ID and rechecked
at sealing and current reads, including status changes; repeated occurrences
still remain in the ordered inventory itself. Full-byte diagnostics reconstruct
the same retained definitions.

## Evidence and limits

Each segment key uses `6529STREAM_SCOPED_RENDER_CRITICAL_SEGMENT_V1`, plan ID and
actual sequential segment index. Every original occurrence enters the existing
ordered item/link chain. The completed evidence uses
`6529STREAM_SCOPED_RENDER_CRITICAL_EVIDENCE_V1`, chain, actual host, dependency
hash and the full scope/evidence tuple with its evidence hash still zero.
Original eight record coordinates, full membership hash/count and complete
segment chain/count enter that tuple. Historical getters do not require current
source eligibility.

The coherent 560-source ABI check includes this host, fixed stages, the scoped
provider and combined profile Discovery. Four token/source
cases and six current-citation cases are authored; none have been run natively
in this scoped batch. The citation tests use actual Membership, Metadata, Schema
and Store, with explicit typed Core, Router/output, Registry and Renderer
admission boundaries. Those tests do not establish governed renderer admission,
an actual current Core ceremony or a fully sealed inventory.

This source producer does not prove archive coverage, independent analysis,
browser/metric execution, opcode conformance, or full finality acceptance.
The fixed scoped archive coverage/provider consumers are implemented in this
batch; their actual complete positive source flow, size and runtime acceptance
remain required. Scoped PERCEPTUAL/CURATED modes and VIEW
adoption retain their distinct required authority and evidence work. All
COLLECTION records, selectors and domains remain unchanged.
